status: DRAFT for Cam to approve (15 Nov 2026). v0.2 with the evidence in coaching_sources.md applied: Toby Radford, the governing-body manuals and the biomechanics research. Items marked "proposed" need Cam's yes or his correction; items marked "agreed in v0.1" are unchanged. IDs C01-C16 keep their meaning where possible, so earlier ratings stay comparable; new checkpoints take new IDs (C17-C19).
scope: Front-foot drive, controlled along the ground, filmed from the bowler's end. Score this shot, not the player.

rating_scale.1: Partly done, or a small fault
rating_scale.X: Cannot judge from this clip (say why)

source_values.Cam: Cam's own coaching notes (WhatsApp, 15 Nov 2026); cam_note keeps his words
source_values.Radford: Toby Radford, as summarised in coaching_sources.md
source_values.consensus: What the governing-body manuals agree on (NZC, ECB, CSA, ICC Europe, Namibia, Discovery Vitality), as summarised in coaching_sources.md
source_values.research: Peer-reviewed biomechanics, as summarised in coaching_sources.md

checkpoints.text: Head level and still at set-up; eyes level
checkpoints.change: none (eyes level was already part of this checkpoint, so it gets no new ID)

checkpoints.text: Balanced base at set-up; weight even, knees relaxed
checkpoints.visible: partly: stance width lies along the pitch

checkpoints.text: As the bowler lets go, the head is over off stump or between middle and off; the eyes are not outside off stump
checkpoints.change: new: Radford checks where the head is, not only whether it is still
checkpoints.measurement: M15 (head over the base at set-up) fits this checkpoint better than C01

checkpoints.text: Hands lift in time to create rhythm (the trigger): the backlift starts early enough to flow into the shot
checkpoints.evidence: Radford: the bat is already going up before the downswing starts. Research: most skilled batters make a trigger movement (Taliep et al. 2007).
checkpoints.change: none since v0.2; wording still to confirm

checkpoints.text: Hands go up and back, close to the body, with the top hand in charge. A bat that lifts out towards the slips is fine: do not mark it down
checkpoints.visible: yes for hands; the bat is not tracked
checkpoints.evidence: Research: most international batters lift the bat towards the slips (Noorbhai & Noakes 2019), so the direction of the backlift is not a fault. Radford: hands close to the body and below the head, top hand leading.
checkpoints.change: a backlift towards the slips is no longer a fault; only a bat that then comes down across the line is, and that is rated at C08

checkpoints.text: Shot choice: the ball is full enough to drive. Rate the choice, not the technique (0 = drove a ball that was too short)
checkpoints.visible: partly: judge the length from where the ball is met; the bounce may be out of shot
checkpoints.change: new: all sources treat the drive as the shot for a full ball, so technique should not take the blame for driving a short one

checkpoints.text: Movement goes out towards the ball, not across the crease
checkpoints.visible: partly: across yes; out towards the bowler no
checkpoints.cam_note: Movement not out towards the ball, movement is across
checkpoints.evidence: Consensus: NZC and coaching pages agree.
checkpoints.change: none since v0.2; wording still to confirm

checkpoints.text: Head and front shoulder lead towards the line of the ball
checkpoints.visible: yes for line; no for forward movement

checkpoints.text: Front foot lands on the line of the ball, or just inside it so the bat has room to come through
checkpoints.evidence: Research: elite batters often land just inside the line (Stuelcken 2005).
checkpoints.change: landing just inside the line is now done well, not a small fault

checkpoints.text: Front knee bends and takes the weight
checkpoints.change: none (the knee-angle measurement is down-weighted; the coach checkpoint stays)

checkpoints.text: Back foot pushes off and the back leg straightens, driving the weight forward into the shot
checkpoints.visible: partly: the back leg is often hidden behind the front leg
checkpoints.change: new: NZC and Discovery Vitality both coach the back-foot push; v0.2 had nothing on the back leg

checkpoints.text: Centre of mass moves out over the ball: weight goes towards the ball, not left behind
checkpoints.cam_note: Centre of mass doesn't move out over the ball
checkpoints.evidence: Consensus and research agree (NZC, Discovery Vitality; weight over the front foot).
checkpoints.change: none since v0.2; wording still to confirm

checkpoints.text: Front shoulder stays aligned to the shot until contact: the top half closes to the line and the chest does not open early. Judge from the stride onwards, not at the stance
checkpoints.visible: yes: the shoulder line narrows as it closes and widens as it opens
checkpoints.evidence: No manual asks for side-on until contact. Radford wants the head and body facing the bowler at release, so side-on is judged only from the stride.
checkpoints.change: was 'body stays side-on until contact'; now the front shoulder stays aligned to the shot, judged from the stride. Takes in Cam's C14 (top half closes), so the same idea is not rated twice

checkpoints.text: Top half closes to give access: front shoulder and chest turn in towards the line, so the hands can reach the ball
checkpoints.visible: yes: the shoulder line narrows as it closes
checkpoints.cam_note: Needs a top half closes access
checkpoints.change: proposed: rate it as part of C07, because closing the top half and keeping the front shoulder aligned are one idea. Not rated on its own in v0.3; the ID is kept so v0.2 ratings stay readable

checkpoints.text: Downswing comes straight through the line of the ball
checkpoints.change: none to the checkpoint; the tip now points to the usual cause (set-up and eye line), from Radford

checkpoints.text: One rhythm from backlift to contact; no pause or hitch. A brief settle of the front foot before the downswing is normal: do not mark it down
checkpoints.evidence: CSA coaches the front foot settling before the downswing. Research: skilled batters land the front foot as the downswing starts (Weissensteiner et al. 2011).
checkpoints.change: a brief settle of the front foot is now named as normal, not a hitch

checkpoints.text: Head over the ball and still at contact; the ball is met close to the front pad, with no wide gap; the head does not fall away
checkpoints.visible: sideways yes; how far forward no
checkpoints.evidence: NZC, Namibia, ICC Europe and research: contact next to the front pad. Radford: contact close to the body, from a still base.
checkpoints.change: adds 'met close to the front pad' and 'still' (the sideways gap is visible from this camera); this replaces a separate contact checkpoint

checkpoints.text: Balance held at the finish; no fall to the off or leg side
Hands continue through towards the target and the finish is controlled. A short, held finish and a full, high finish are both fine; hands that stop at contact or a wild swing are not
checkpoints.change: a short, controlled finish is no longer a fault (v0.1 marked down a 'checked' finish)

not_judged_from_this_camera: Stride length and weight forward (depth along the pitch)
Front knee ahead of the toes (depth)
How far in front of the eyes the ball is met (the sideways gap to the pad is judged at C10)
Bat face and whether the full face goes to the target
Timing and where the ball went

faults_in_chain_order.text: Head moves early or is not still at set-up
Head out of position as the bowler lets go: eyes outside off stump
Hands late or static: no rhythm from the backlift
Hands go out away from the body in the backlift
Drives a ball that is too short to drive
Moves across the crease, not out towards the ball
Head and shoulder do not lead to the line
Front foot well away from the line of the ball
Front leg stiff; weight stays back
Back foot stays put: no push to drive the weight forward
Centre of mass stays back: does not move out over the ball
Front shoulder opens early, or the top half never closes
Pause or hitch in the swing
Head falls away at contact, or the ball is met away from the pad
Hands stop at contact, or the follow-through is wild

faults_retired.text: Top half stays open: no access to the ball

priority_fix_rule: Pick ONE fault: the one that, fixed first, would help this player most. This is usually the earliest fault in the chain, because later faults often follow from it. If the ball was too short to drive (C19 = 0), give F19 and do not blame the technique for the result.

access.5: Plays across the line: foot well away from the line, chest open early, hands out wide
access.15: Gets near the line, but opens a little early or the hands drift
access.25: Foot on or just inside the line, front shoulder aligned to the shot until contact, hands straight through the line

tracking.5: Head moves early, sits outside off stump and falls away at contact
tracking.15: Head mostly still, leads late, drifts a little at contact
tracking.25: Still, level head over off stump that leads to the line and stays over the ball

stability.5: Unbalanced from set-up, falls away at the finish
stability.15: Balanced, but the weight stays back or the finish wobbles
stability.25: Balanced base, back foot drives the weight onto a bent front knee, finish held

flow.5: Stop-start: late backlift, pause at the top, hands stop at contact
flow.25: One smooth rhythm from an early backlift to a controlled finish

score_sheet_notes.checkpoints: The 18 rated checkpoints, in chain order. C14 is not a column in v0.3: it is rated as part of C07.
score_sheet_notes.overall: Score it on its own (0-100); do not add up the pillars. Phase 2 tests whether coaches overall equals the pillar sum.
